text: Both views are in Power BI now. This lesson turns one of them into Support's actual page — built to answer, at a glance, exactly what Support asked for back in Lesson 1.

A line chart, ticket_week on the X-axis, ticket_count on the Y, split by category as the legend — is volume trending up or down, and which categories are driving it. A table, sorted by opened_at ascending, surfaces the oldest still-open tickets at the top, the ones most likely to need attention first.

Two slicers, category and priority, filter both the trend chart and the open-tickets table together. This is the real self-service pattern Support asked for: a page they can slice themselves, without asking anyone to re-run a query.

Notice there's no DAX measure anywhere on this page yet. ticket_count was already aggregated with COUNT star back in the Snowflake view itself. Power BI's automatic Sum of ticket_count re-aggregates that correctly by default — writing a custom measure here would just be one more place a mistake could hide, for no real benefit.
Support's page is done. Next lesson builds Finance's page, on the exact same shared foundation, shaped for a completely different audience.
